{{MedalSilver|[[FIBA Oceania Championship 2009|2009 Australia/New Zealand]]|}} }} '''Aron John Baynes''' (born 9 December 1986) is an Australian former professional [[basketball]] player. He played [[college basketball]] for [[Washington State Cougars men's basketball|Washington State University]] before starting his professional career in Europe. In 2013, he joined the [[San Antonio Spurs]], and a year later, won an [[List of NBA champions|NBA championship]] with the Spurs. He has also played with the [[Detroit Pistons]], [[Boston Celtics]], [[Phoenix Suns]] and [[Toronto Raptors]]. In the [[National Basketball League (Australia)|National Basketball League]] (NBL), he played for the [[Brisbane Bullets]] between 2022 and 2024. Baynes also played for the [[Australia men's national basketball team|Australian national team]]. ==Early life== Baynes was born in [[Gisborne, New Zealand]] to [[New Zealanders|New Zealand]] parents in 1986.{{cite web |last1=Egan |first1=Brendon |title=Aussie NBA rookie mistakenly credited to NZ |url=http://www.stuff.co.nz/sport/8264483/Aussie-NBA-rookie-mistakenly-credited-to-NZ |website=Stuff |access-date=19 October 2020 |language=en |date=6 February 2013}} His family moved to the small Australian town of [[Mareeba]], [[Queensland, Australia|Queensland]] when he was three years of age.{{cite news |url=https://www.couriermail.com.au/sport/us-sports/nba/aron-baynes-is-the-last-aussie-left-in-the-nba-but-now-faces-the-monster-task-of-lebron-james/news-story/3061f6894949727d17c7292ee064f65a |title=Aron Baynes is the last Aussie left in the NBA – but now faces the monster task of LeBron James |first=Greg |last=Davis |date=12 May 2018 |newspaper=The Courier-Mail |access-date=12 May 2020}}[http://www.nzherald.co.nz/hawkes-bay-today/sport/news/article.cfm?c_id=1503460&objectid=10939354 Baynes and bro' not doing a Hunt] He grew up playing [[rugby league]] in [[Far North Queensland]] while attending [[Mareeba State High School]] until the age of 15 when his older brother, Callum, introduced him to basketball.{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/spurs/features/130404_rodriguez_baynes |title=Improbable Journey From Down Under |website=Spurs.com}} As a result, Baynes decided to focus on pursuing a career in basketball and subsequently quit rugby league. Shortly after high school graduation, he joined the [[Australian Institute of Sport]] in 2004–05 and accepted a college scholarship offer from [[Tony Bennett (basketball)|Tony Bennett]] to play for [[Washington State University]] in 2006.[https://247sports.com/college/washington-state/Article/Bennett-Baynes-a-man-of-many-faces-104561739 Bennett: Baynes a man of many faces], accessed 1 March 2018 During his college career under Bennett, Washington State tied the school wins record twice consecutively, going 26–8 in 2006–07 and 26–9 in 2007–08. ==Professional career== ===Europe (2009–2013)=== On 29 May 2009, Baynes signed a two-year deal with [[BC Lietuvos rytas|Lietuvos Rytas]] of the [[Lietuvos krepšinio lyga|Lithuanian Basketball League]].{{cite web |url=http://www.sportando.com/en/cups/euroleague/77087/lietuvos-rytas-goes-big-with-baynes.html |title=Lietuvos Rytas goes big with Baynes}}{{cite web |url=https://www.euroleaguebasketball.net/eurocup/news/ |title=Lietuvos Rytas tabs center Baynes|date=6 December 2024 }} In July 2009, he played for the [[Los Angeles Lakers]]' Summer League team. Following the 2009–10 season, he parted ways with Lietuvos Rytas.{{cite web |url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/lithuania/81718/five-players-will-leave-lietuvos-rytas.html |title=Five players will leave Lietuvos Rytas}} On 15 July 2010, Baynes signed a two-year deal with [[EWE Baskets Oldenburg]] of the German [[Basketball Bundesliga]].{{cite web |url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/germany/83219/aron-baynes-inks-with-oldenburg.html |title=Aron Baynes inks with Oldenburg}} In 40 games for Oldenburg in 2010–11, he averaged 6.8 points and 3.7 rebounds per game. On 29 June 2011, he parted ways with Oldenburg.{{cite web |url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/germany/86875/aaron-baynes-leaves-oldenburg.html |title=Aaron Baynes leaves Oldenburg |access-date=1 December 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141207054510/http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/germany/86875/aaron-baynes-leaves-oldenburg.html |archive-date=7 December 2014 |url-status=dead}} On 24 August 2011, Baynes signed a one-year deal with [[Ikaros Kallitheas B.C.|Ikaros Kallitheas]] of the [[Greek Basket League]].{{cite web |url=http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/greece/88206/ikaros-gets-aron-bynes.html |title=Ikaros gets Aron Bynes |access-date=1 December 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20141207054616/http://www.sportando.com/en/europe/greece/88206/ikaros-gets-aron-bynes.html |archive-date=7 December 2014 |url-status=dead}} On 1 August 2012, Baynes signed a one-year deal with [[KK Union Olimpija|Union Olimpija]] of the [[Premier A Slovenian Basketball League|Slovenian Basketball League]].{{cite web |url=http://www.euroleague.net/news/i/99034/union-olimpija-also-lands-baynes |title=Union Olimpija also lands Baynes |work=Euroleague.net |date=1 August 2012 |access-date=9 September 2012}} On 5 January 2013, he played his final game for Olimpija, as he later left the team in pursuit of an NBA contract.{{cite web |url=http://www.sportando.com/en/usa/nba/98184/aron-baynes-close-to-sign-a-multi-year-deal-with-the-spurs.html |title=Aron Baynes close to sign a multi-year deal with the Spurs}} ===San Antonio Spurs (2013–2015)=== On 23 January 2013, Baynes signed with the [[San Antonio Spurs]].{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/spurs/news/130123_spurs_sign_aron_baynes |title=Spurs Sign Aron Baynes - San Antonio Spurs |website=[[NBA.com]]}} In his second NBA game, Baynes recorded seven points, nine rebounds and one block in a 102–78 win over the [[Charlotte Bobcats]].{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20130130/CHASAS/gameinfo.html |title=Bobcats at Spurs |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=31 January 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171107044459/http://www.nba.com/games/20130130/CHASAS/gameinfo.html |archive-date=7 November 2017 |url-status=dead}} During the 2012–13 season, he was assigned multiple times to the [[Austin Toros]] of the [[NBA G League]].{{cite web |url=http://origin.nba.com/dleague/assignments_2012_13.html |title=NBA Development League: 2012–13 NBA Assignments |website=origin.nba.com |access-date=15 November 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190422224439/http://origin.nba.com/dleague/assignments_2012_13.html |archive-date=22 April 2019 |url-status=dead}} He made his first NBA start in Game 4 of the Spurs' first-round playoff match-up against the [[Los Angeles Lakers]], and was tasked with defending [[Dwight Howard]].{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20130428/SASLAL/gameinfo.html |title=Spurs at Lakers |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=2 May 2013 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190602154027/https://www.nba.com/games/20130428/SASLAL/gameinfo.html |archive-date=2 June 2019 |url-status=dead}} The Spurs went on to reach the [[2013 NBA Finals]] but lost the series in seven games to the [[Miami Heat]]. [[File:Aron Baynes and Patty Mills in front of the ACT Legislative Assembly in July 2014.png|thumb|left|Baynes (left) and teammate [[Patty Mills]] in July 2014, with the NBA Championship trophy.]] On 1 December 2013, Baynes was reassigned to the Austin Toros.{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/spurs/news/131201_baynes_decolo_assigned_to_toros |title=Spurs Assign Baynes and De Colo to Austin Toros - San Antonio Spurs |website=[[NBA.com]]}} He was recalled on 2 December,{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/spurs/news/131202_baynes_decolo |title=Spurs Recall Baynes and De Colo - San Antonio Spurs |website=[[NBA.com]]}} reassigned on 8 December,{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/spurs/news/131208_spurs_assign_baynes_decolo_thomas_to_toros |title=Spurs Assign Baynes, De Colo and Thomas to Toros - San Antonio Spurs |website=[[NBA.com]]}} and recalled again on 9 December.{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/spurs/news/131209_baynes_decolo_recalled |title=Spurs Recall Baynes and De Colo from Toros - San Antonio Spurs |website=[[NBA.com]]}} On 6 May 2014, he recorded playoff career-high numbers of 10 points and seven rebounds in a 116–92 win over the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] in Game 1 of the Western Conference semi-finals.{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400556334 |title=Trail Blazers vs. Spurs - Game Recap - May 6, 2014 - ESPN |website=ESPN.com}} Baynes went on to help the Spurs defeat the Miami Heat 4–1 in the [[2014 NBA Finals]] to claim his first NBA championship. On 26 September 2014, Baynes re-signed with the Spurs.{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/spurs/news/140926_spurs_re_sign_aron_bayne |title=Spurs Re-Sign Aron Baynes - San Antonio Spurs |website=[[NBA.com]]}} On 20 December 2014, he scored a then career-high 16 points while starting in place of [[Tim Duncan]] in a 99–93 loss to the [[Dallas Mavericks]].{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20141220/SASDAL/gameinfo.html |title=Spurs at Mavericks |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=21 December 2014 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180205193709/http://www.nba.com/games/20141220/SASDAL/gameinfo.html |archive-date=5 February 2018 |url-status=dead}} On 1 April 2015 and 3 April 2015, Baynes had back-to-back 18-point games.{{cite web |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/b/baynear01/gamelog/2015/ |title=Aron Baynes 2014-15 Game Log - Basketball-Reference.com |website=Basketball-Reference.com}} ===Detroit Pistons (2015–2017)=== [[File:Aron Baynes, John Wall (31692356675).jpg|thumb|right|Baynes guards [[John Wall]] in 2016]] On 12 July 2015, Baynes signed with the [[Detroit Pistons]].{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/pistons/news/detroit-pistons-sign-center-aron-baynes |title=Detroit Pistons Sign Center Aron Baynes |work=NBA.com |date=12 July 2015 |access-date=12 July 2015}} On 19 March 2016, he scored a career-high 21 points in a 115–103 win over the [[Brooklyn Nets]].{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160319/BKNDET/gameinfo.html |title=Nets vs Pistons |website=[[NBA.com]] |access-date=20 March 2016 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160320201050/http://www.nba.com/games/20160319/BKNDET/gameinfo.html |archive-date=20 March 2016 |url-status=dead}} On 14 November 2016, Baynes scored 20 points against the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] while starting in place of [[Andre Drummond]].{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899597 |title=Thunder vs. Pistons - Game Recap - November 14, 2016 - ESPN |website=ESPN.com}} On 19 March 2017, Baynes grabbed a career-high 17 rebounds alongside 13 points in a 112–95 win over the [[Phoenix Suns]].{{Cite web |title=Phoenix Suns at Detroit Pistons Box Score, March 19, 2017 |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/boxscores/201703190DET.html |access-date=2021-04-13 |website=Basketball-Reference.com |language=en}} ===Boston Celtics (2017–2019)=== On 19 July 2017, Baynes signed with the [[Boston Celtics]].{{cite web |url=http://www.nba.com/celtics/news/pressrelease/boston-celtics-sign-aron-baynes |title=Boston Celtics Sign Aron Baynes |work=NBA.com |date=19 July 2017 |access-date=19 July 2017}} In a game against the [[Charlotte Hornets]], Baynes injured Celtics teammate and star [[point guard]] [[Kyrie Irving]]. On 8 November 2017, he matched his career high with 21 points in a 107–96 win over the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400974912 |title=Baynes lifts Celtics over Lakers for 10th straight win |work=ESPN.com |date=8 November 2017 |access-date=8 November 2017}} In the Celtics' regular season finale on 11 April 2018, Baynes led a short-handed Boston lineup with a career-best 26 points and 14 rebounds in a 110–97 win over the [[Brooklyn Nets]].{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400975965 |title=Baynes 26 points, 14 rebounds leads Celtics past Nets |work=ESPN.com |date=11 April 2018 |access-date=11 April 2018}} On 7 July 2018, Baynes re-signed with the Celtics.{{cite web |url=https://www.nba.com/celtics/news/pressrelease/celtics-re-sign-aron-baynes |title=Celtics Re-Sign Aron Baynes |website=NBA.com |date=7 July 2018 |access-date=9 July 2018}} On 19 December 2018, in a 111–103 loss to the [[Phoenix Suns]], Baynes broke a bone in his left hand.{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071139 |title=Booker, Ayton carry Suns past Celtics for 4th straight win |work=ESPN.com |date=19 December 2018 |access-date=19 December 2018}} He was subsequently ruled out for four to six weeks.{{cite web |url=https://www.nba.com/celtics/news/pressrelease/aron-baynes-injury-update |title=Aron Baynes Injury Update |work=NBA.com |date=20 December 2018 |access-date=22 December 2018}} He returned to action on 16 January 2019 against the [[Toronto Raptors]].{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401071334 |title=Irving's 27 points, 18 assists leads Celtics past Raptors |work=ESPN.com |date=16 January 2019 |access-date=17 January 2019}} On 3 February, he was sidelined with a left foot contusion.{{cite web |last=Randall |first=Dakota |url=https://nesn.com/2019/02/aron-baynes-injury-celtics-center-to-miss-few-weeks-with-foot-contusion/ |title=Aron Baynes Injury: Celtics Center To Miss 'Few Weeks' With Foot Contusion |work=nesn.com |date=3 February 2019 |access-date=3 February 2019}} ===Phoenix Suns (2019–2020)=== On 6 July 2019, Baynes, along with the draft rights to [[Ty Jerome]], was traded to the [[Phoenix Suns]] for a 2020 protected first-round pick.{{cite web |title=Celtics Complete Trade With Phoenix Suns |url=https://www.nba.com/celtics/news/pressrelease/celtics-complete-trade-phoenix-suns |website=NBA.com |access-date=6 July 2019 |date=6 July 2019}} After [[Deandre Ayton]] was suspended for 25 games due to [[diuretic]] usage on 24 October, Baynes was promoted to being the team's starting center during that period of time. On 30 October, Baynes recorded 24 points, 12 rebounds, and a career-high 7 assists in a 121–110 win over the [[Golden State Warriors]].{{cite web |first=Janie |last=McCauley |url=https://www.nba.com/games/20191030/PHXGSW#/boxscore |title=Curry breaks left hand in another embarrassing Warriors loss |website=NBA.com |date=31 October 2019 |access-date=9 December 2019}} On 6 March 2020, Baynes scored 37 points and hit nine three-pointers, both career-highs, along with 16 rebounds, in a 127–117 victory over the [[Portland Trail Blazers]].{{Cite web |last= |first= |date=2020-03-07 |title=Watch Aron Baynes score career-high 37 points, lift Suns past Trail Blazers |url=https://nba.nbcsports.com/2020/03/07/aron-baynes-career-high-37/ |access-date=2021-04-13 |url=https://arizonasports.com/story/2284909/aron-baynes-scores-37-points-as-suns-win-25th-game-of-the-season/ |access-date=2021-04-13 |website=Arizona Sports}} He not only tied a franchise record for most three-pointers made in a single game, but he also joins [[James Harden]] as the only other player to record 35+ points, 15+ rebounds, and 9 three-pointers in a single game.{{cite web |url=https://twitter.com/ESPNStatsInfo/status/1236166845754941440 |title=Aron Baynes had 37 pts, 16 reb, and 9 Three-Pointers tonight in the Suns 127-117 win over the Trailblazers Boston.com|url=https://www.boston.com/sports/nba/2020/03/07/aron-baynes-phoenix-suns-career-high/|access-date=2021-04-13|website=www.boston.com|language=en-US}} On 23 June 2020, the Suns reported that two of their own players tested positive for [[COVID-19]].{{cite web |first=Duane |last=Rankin |url=https://www.azcentral.com/story/sports/nba/suns/2020/06/23/two-phoenix-suns-players-have-tested-positive-coronavirus-sources-say/3240663001/ |title=Two Phoenix Suns players tested positive for COVID-19, sources say |website=AZCentral.com |date=23 June 2020 |access-date=1 August 2020}} In an interview on 22 July, Baynes revealed himself as one of the two players to test positive for COVID-19.{{cite web |first=Duane |last=Rankin |url=https://www.azcentral.com/story/sports/nba/suns/2020/07/22/rubio-back-aron-baynes-not-suns-vets-tested-positive-covid-19/5489420002/ |title=Ricky Rubio back, Aron Baynes not as Phoenix Suns veterans tested positive for COVID-19 |website=AZCentral.com |date=22 July 2020 |access-date=1 August 2020}} Unlike his other teammate that tested positive, Baynes did not rejoin the team in the [[2020 NBA Bubble]] until after the scrimmage games were finished, making sure he completely tested negative for the virus before entering the bubble. Because of his late entry and subsequent [[quarantine]] period, he was not able to play on 31 July against the [[Washington Wizards]].{{cite web |url=https://www.nba.com/games/20200731/PHXWAS/#/recap |title=Booker scores 27 points, Suns beat Wizards 125-112 in return |website=NBA.com |date=31 July 2020 |access-date=1 August 2020}} After recovering from the virus, Baynes was later diagnosed with a right knee contusion, leaving him out of action for the rest of the resumed regular season.{{Cite web |date=August 5, 2020 |title=Injury Report: 08/05/20 05:30 PM {{!}} NBA|url=https://ak-static.cms.nba.com/referee/injury/Injury-Report_2020-08-05_05PM.pdf}} Despite being out of action for most of the game, Baynes was considered clear to play for the team's last game of the season, but decided against it despite the blowout 128–102 win over the [[Dallas Mavericks]], ending the resumed season with an 8–0 record.{{cite web |date=13 August 2020 |title=Suns top Mavs to keep playoff hopes alive, go 8-0 in bubble |url=https://www.nba.com/games/20200813/DALPHX/#/recap |access-date=13 August 2020 |website=NBA.com}} ===Toronto Raptors (2020–2021)=== On 25 November 2020, the [[Toronto Raptors]] signed Baynes to a multi-year contract.{{cite web |title=Raptors Sign Baynes |url=https://www.nba.com/raptors/raptors-sign-baynes |date=25 November 2020 |access-date=25 November 2020 |website=NBA.com}} On 31 January 2021, Baynes had eight points and a season-high 16 rebounds in a 115–102 win against the [[Orlando Magic]].{{cite web |title=Raptors snap 3-game losing streak, beat Raptors 115-102 |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=401267469 |website=ESPN.com |date=31 January 2021 |access-date=2 February 2021}} On 4 August 2021, he was waived by the Raptors.{{cite web |first=Luke |last=Adams |title=Raptors Waive Aron Baynes |url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2021/08/raptors-waive-aron-baynes.html |website=HoopsRumors.com |date=4 August 2021 |access-date=4 August 2021}} ===Brisbane Bullets (2022–2024)=== After suffering a career-threatening spinal cord injury during the Tokyo Olympics, Baynes returned to professional basketball by signing a two-year deal with the [[Brisbane Bullets]] of the [[National Basketball League (Australia)|National Basketball League]] on 28 July 2022.{{cite web |author=Brain Windhorst |title=Aron Baynes to play for NBL's Brisbane Bullets with goal of returning to NBA |url=https://www.espn.com.au/nba/story/_/id/34303087/aron-baynes-play-nbl-brisbane-bullets-goal-returning-nba |website=ESPN.com.au |date=27 July 2022 |access-date=28 July 2022}}{{cite web |title=Aron Baynes Comeback Complete |url=https://nbl.com.au/news/aron-baynes-comeback-complete |website=NBL.com.au |date=28 July 2022 |access-date=28 July 2022}} In a match on October 7, 2023, against [[Cairns Taipans]], Baynes was handed a five-game suspension for unsportsmanlike conduct, unacceptable basketball act and excessive disputing following his ejection from the match.{{Cite web |last=Pavlou |first=Anna |date=2023-10-15 |title=NBL slams 'disheartening' breach after altercation |url=https://wwos.nine.com.au/basketball/news-2023-nbl-slams-security-leak-footage-of-altercation-between-aron-baynes-adam-forde/a04e7a34-f73c-4982-ae78-00aa30dcffe3 |access-date=2023-10-16 |website=Nine.com.au |language=en}} Despite being the highest paid player in the [[2023–24 NBL season]], at 37 years old, he averaged only 13 minutes a game over the first half of the season.{{cite web |title=The teams who could spend big in NBL25 |url=https://nbl.com.au/news/the-teams-who-could-spend-big-in-nbl25 |website=NBL.com.au |date=31 December 2023 |access-date=31 December 2023 |quote=...Aron Baynes, he's the highest paid player in the league this season...}} On 17 October 2024, Baynes announced his retirement from basketball.{{cite news|title=NBA champion Aron Baynes retires|url=https://www.espn.com.au/nbl/story/_/id/41835842/australian-basketball-star-nba-champion-aron-baynes-retires|website=ESPN.com.au|date=17 October 2024|access-date=17 October 2024}} ==National team career== Baynes has played for the [[Australia men's national basketball team|Australian national team]], the Boomers, at the [[2010 FIBA World Championship]] in Turkey, the [[Basketball at the 2012 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2012 Summer Olympics]] in London,{{cite web |url=http://london2012.fiba.com/pages/eng/fe/12/olym/player/p/eid/6232/pid/52781/sid/6232/tid/239/profile.html |title=Aron Baynes – 2012 Olympic Men |access-date=12 August 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121001180026/http://london2012.fiba.com/pages/eng/fe/12/olym/player/p/eid/6232/pid/52781/sid/6232/tid/239/profile.html |archive-date=1 October 2012
